analysis:
This batch contains documentation only. It adds changelog.d/installer-release-file-modes.md, lines 1-3. It also changes docs/operations/provider-release.md at head line 3 (date) and head lines 411-414.

The new text says scripts/install.sh (install_bundle_atomically) extracts the release archive with /usr/bin/tar under umask 022. Installed app files therefore become group/world-readable, with no group/world write bits, instead of owner-only. Private state is said to keep its own modes.

Security relevance: this touches TB-003 and T-013, the operator-versus-process boundary for binary tampering. Under umask 022 the default mode is 0755 for directories and 0644 for files. That adds read access only, not write access, so a narrower umask was never a confidentiality control for signed public release bytes. Code-signature verification (verify_staged_app_signature) and the TB-011 qualification remain the integrity controls.

The actual scripts/install.sh change is not in this batch. Integration must verify the following:
- umask 022 is scoped to the extraction subshell only. It must not leak to later creation of provider.toml, token or credential files (A-008), keychain-adjacent state, or encrypted cache directories (T-041). Those must keep owner-only modes.
- tar extraction does not preserve attacker-controlled archive modes (setuid, world-writable) or ownership. The flags used must be checked, e.g. no -p when running as root.
- an absolute /usr/bin/tar is used, which avoids PATH hijack.
- signature/hash verification of the bin/ files still runs before atomic install.

No regression is evidenced from the documentation alone.
